questions.question: What was the first permanent English settlement in North America?
questions.correctAnswer: Jamestown, Virginia
distractors: Plymouth, Massachusetts
Roanoke, Virginia
St. Augustine, Florida
questions.explanation: Jamestown was founded in 1607 by the Virginia Company and survived to become the first permanent English settlement, while Roanoke was lost.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Jamestown in 1607 - jam your feet in the mud and stay put, the first town that stuck!

questions.question: What document did the Pilgrims sign aboard ship in 1620 to agree to self-government?
questions.correctAnswer: The Mayflower Compact
distractors: The Fundamental Orders
The House of Burgesses
The Virginia Charter
questions.explanation: The Mayflower Compact was signed in 1620 before landing at Plymouth and established a civil body politic based on majority rule.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Mayflower Compact - a compact promise on a cramped ship to govern themselves!

questions.question: In what year was the Declaration of Independence adopted?
questions.explanation: The Continental Congress adopted the Declaration of Independence on July 4, 1776, formally breaking with Britain.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1776 - seven, seven, six, independence clicks!

questions.question: Who was the first President of the United States?
questions.correctAnswer: George Washington
distractors: John Adams
Thomas Jefferson
Benjamin Franklin
questions.explanation: George Washington was unanimously elected and served from 1789 to 1797, setting many presidential precedents.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Washington first - the general who became president number one!

questions.question: In which years was the American Civil War fought?
questions.explanation: The Civil War began with the attack on Fort Sumter in April 1861 and ended with Lee's surrender at Appomattox in April 1865.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 61 to 65 - four hard years that split and healed the nation!

questions.question: Who issued the Emancipation Proclamation?
questions.correctAnswer: Abraham Lincoln
distractors: Ulysses S. Grant
Andrew Johnson
Jefferson Davis
questions.explanation: Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863, freeing enslaved people in Confederate-held territory.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lincoln's proclamation - the pen that proclaimed freedom in 63!

questions.question: What event brought the United States into World War II?
questions.correctAnswer: The attack on Pearl Harbor
distractors: The sinking of the Lusitania
The Zimmermann Telegram
The invasion of Poland
questions.explanation: Japan's surprise attack on Pearl Harbor on December 7, 1941 led Congress to declare war the next day.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pearl Harbor, December 7 - a day that woke a sleeping giant!

questions.question: The Cold War was primarily a rivalry between the United States and which country?
questions.correctAnswer: The Soviet Union
distractors: Germany
China
Japan
questions.explanation: The Cold War (roughly 1947-1991) pitted the capitalist United States against the communist Soviet Union without direct large-scale war between them.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Cold War - two superpowers, icy stares, no direct fight!

questions.question: Who delivered the famous 'I Have a Dream' speech in 1963?
questions.correctAnswer: Martin Luther King Jr.
distractors: Malcolm X
Rosa Parks
John F. Kennedy
questions.explanation: King delivered the speech at the March on Washington for Jobs and Freedom on August 28, 1963.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: King had a dream - jobs, freedom, and equality for all!

questions.question: What was the Boston Tea Party a protest against?
questions.correctAnswer: British taxes on tea
distractors: British bans on newspapers
British troops in Boston
British control of trade with France
questions.explanation: In December 1773, colonists dumped tea into Boston Harbor to protest the Tea Act and taxation without representation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tea in the harbor - taxed tea makes salty water!

questions.question: In what year was the U.S. Constitution ratified?
questions.explanation: The Constitution was ratified in 1788 when New Hampshire became the ninth state to approve it, and it took effect in 1789.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1788 - eight ate eight states, then one more made it law!

questions.question: Which president bought the Louisiana Territory from France in 1803?
questions.correctAnswer: Thomas Jefferson
distractors: James Madison
John Adams
James Monroe
questions.explanation: Jefferson's purchase doubled the size of the United States for about 15 million dollars.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Jefferson's bargain - fifteen million for half a continent!

questions.question: What was the Trail of Tears?
questions.correctAnswer: The forced removal of Cherokee and other Native peoples westward
distractors: A gold rush route to California
A cattle trail to Texas
A pioneer wagon road to Oregon
questions.explanation: Under the Indian Removal Act, thousands of Cherokee died on the forced march to Oklahoma in 1838-1839.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Trail of Tears - a forced march west that left tears on every mile!

questions.question: Where did Lincoln deliver the Gettysburg Address in 1863?
questions.correctAnswer: At the dedication of a soldiers' cemetery in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania
distractors: At his second inauguration in Washington
At the signing of the Emancipation Proclamation
At the surrender at Appomattox
questions.explanation: Lincoln's brief address at the Gettysburg battlefield cemetery redefined the war as a struggle for equality and democracy.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gettysburg - 272 words that rededicated a nation!

questions.question: Which amendment gave women the right to vote?
questions.correctAnswer: The 19th Amendment
distractors: The 15th Amendment
The 17th Amendment
The 21st Amendment
questions.explanation: The 19th Amendment, ratified in 1920, prohibited denying the vote on account of sex.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 19 in 1920 - women win the vote at last!

questions.question: What event is generally seen as starting the Great Depression?
questions.correctAnswer: The stock market crash of October 1929
distractors: The Dust Bowl of 1934
The bank failures of 1933
The Smoot-Hawley Tariff of 1930
questions.explanation: The crash of October 1929 shattered confidence and helped trigger a decade of depression, though deeper causes included overproduction and weak banking.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Black Tuesday 1929 - stocks crashed and the decade went dark!

questions.question: Whose New Deal programs responded to the Great Depression?
questions.correctAnswer: Franklin D. Roosevelt
distractors: Herbert Hoover
Calvin Coolidge
Harry Truman
questions.explanation: FDR's New Deal (1933-1939) used federal programs like the CCC, TVA, and Social Security to provide relief, recovery, and reform.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: FDR's New Deal - relief, recovery, reform, three Rs to the rescue!

questions.question: In what year did American astronauts first land on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969, with Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walking on its surface.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1969 - one small step for man, one giant leap for mankind!

questions.question: Which amendment abolished slavery in the United States?
questions.correctAnswer: The 13th Amendment
distractors: The 12th Amendment
The 14th Amendment
The 15th Amendment
questions.explanation: The 13th Amendment, ratified in 1865, abolished slavery and involuntary servitude except as punishment for a crime.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 13 ends slavery - unlucky number, lucky freedom!

questions.question: What did the Monroe Doctrine of 1823 declare?
questions.correctAnswer: European powers should not colonize or interfere in the Americas
distractors: The United States would annex Texas
Britain would defend Latin America
The United States would stay out of all foreign wars
questions.explanation: President Monroe warned Europe against further colonization in the Western Hemisphere, a policy later backed by British naval power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Monroe's warning - hands off the Americas, Europe!

questions.question: Which war began in 1898 after the explosion of the USS Maine?
questions.correctAnswer: The Spanish-American War
distractors: The Mexican-American War
World War I
The Philippine-American War
questions.explanation: The Spanish-American War (1898) resulted in U.S. control of Puerto Rico, Guam, and the Philippines and Cuban independence.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Remember the Maine - 1898, Spain loses an empire!

questions.question: The Vietnam War ended for the United States in 1973 with what agreement?
questions.correctAnswer: The Paris Peace Accords
distractors: The Geneva Accords
The Camp David Accords
The SALT Treaty
questions.explanation: The Paris Peace Accords of January 1973 ended direct U.S. military involvement in Vietnam, though fighting continued until Saigon fell in 1975.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Paris 1973 - the accords that brought the troops home!

questions.question: What scandal led to President Nixon's resignation in 1974?
questions.correctAnswer: Watergate
distractors: Iran-Contra
Teapot Dome
The Pentagon Papers
questions.explanation: The Watergate break-in cover-up led to impeachment proceedings, and Nixon resigned on August 9, 1974.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Watergate - a break-in and a cover-up that sank a presidency!

questions.question: What are the first ten amendments to the Constitution called?
questions.correctAnswer: The Bill of Rights
distractors: The Federalist Papers
The Articles of Confederation
The Reconstruction Amendments
questions.explanation: The Bill of Rights, ratified in 1791, protects freedoms of speech, religion, press, and other individual rights.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bill of Rights - ten amendments, ten shields for freedom!

questions.question: What were the Federalist Papers?
questions.correctAnswer: Essays supporting ratification of the Constitution
distractors: The first laws passed by Congress
Anti-British pamphlets from 1776
The Supreme Court's first decisions
questions.explanation: Hamilton, Madison, and Jay wrote 85 essays in 1787-1788 arguing for the new Constitution, published as The Federalist.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Federalist Papers - 85 essays that sold the Constitution!

questions.question: Who led the Corps of Discovery expedition to the Pacific in 1804-1806?
questions.correctAnswer: Meriwether Lewis and William Clark
distractors: Zebulon Pike and John Fremont
Daniel Boone and Davy Crockett
John Smith and John Rolfe
questions.explanation: Lewis and Clark explored the Louisiana Purchase and reached the Pacific, mapping the route and meeting Native nations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lewis and Clark - two captains, one river, all the way to the Pacific!

questions.question: In what year was the transcontinental railroad completed at Promontory, Utah?
questions.explanation: The Central Pacific and Union Pacific met at Promontory Summit on May 10, 1869, linking east and west by rail.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Golden spike 1869 - east meets west on iron rails!

questions.question: Ellis Island in New York Harbor was mainly used for what purpose?
questions.correctAnswer: Processing immigrants arriving in the United States
distractors: Quarantining sick soldiers
Housing freed slaves
Training naval officers
questions.explanation: From 1892 to 1954, Ellis Island processed millions of immigrants, most from Europe, before they entered the country.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Ellis Island - the gateway where millions became Americans!

questions.question: What did Brown v. Board of Education (1954) decide?
questions.correctAnswer: Segregated public schools are unconstitutional
distractors: Prayer in schools is unconstitutional
Busing students is unconstitutional
Affirmative action is unconstitutional
questions.explanation: The unanimous decision overturned Plessy v. Ferguson's 'separate but equal' doctrine in public education.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Brown 1954 - separate is inherently unequal!

questions.question: Which battle is considered the turning point of the Civil War in the East?
questions.correctAnswer: Gettysburg
distractors: Bull Run
Antietam
Vicksburg
questions.explanation: The Union victory at Gettysburg in July 1863 ended Lee's invasion of the North and, with Vicksburg, marked the war's turning point.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gettysburg July 1863 - Pickett's charge fails, the tide turns!

questions.question: What was the main weakness of the Articles of Confederation?
questions.correctAnswer: The central government had no power to tax or enforce laws
distractors: It gave too much power to the president
It banned slavery in all states
It required unanimous consent for all laws
questions.explanation: Under the Articles, Congress could not tax, regulate commerce, or enforce its decisions, which led to the Constitutional Convention of 1787.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Articles - a government that could ask but never command!

questions.question: What did the Great Compromise of 1787 decide?
questions.correctAnswer: Congress would have a House based on population and a Senate with equal state representation
distractors: Slavery would be banned after 1808
The president would serve four-year terms
The capital would move to Washington, D.C.
questions.explanation: The Connecticut Compromise blended the Virginia Plan (population) and New Jersey Plan (equal states) into the bicameral Congress.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Great Compromise - big states get the House, small states get the Senate!

questions.question: What was the core of Alexander Hamilton's financial plan?
questions.correctAnswer: The federal government would assume state debts and create a national bank
distractors: The government would abolish all tariffs
The government would pay off debts with new land sales only
The government would coin money from silver alone
questions.explanation: Hamilton's plan funded the national debt, assumed state debts, and chartered the Bank of the United States to build credit and commerce.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hamilton's plan - assume the debt, bank the future!

questions.question: What did the Whiskey Rebellion of 1794 demonstrate?
questions.correctAnswer: The federal government would enforce its laws with force if needed
distractors: Farmers could refuse to pay any taxes
The president could not command troops
Western states could secede freely
questions.explanation: Washington led troops to suppress Pennsylvania farmers protesting the whiskey tax, showing federal authority under the new Constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Whiskey Rebellion - Washington marches west and the tax sticks!

questions.question: What principle did Marbury v. Madison (1803) establish?
questions.correctAnswer: Judicial review, the Court's power to declare laws unconstitutional
distractors: The president's power to veto Court decisions
The states' right to nullify federal law
The Senate's power to confirm judges
questions.explanation: Chief Justice John Marshall asserted that the Supreme Court could strike down laws conflicting with the Constitution.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Marbury - Marshall grabs the gavel and claims judicial review!

questions.question: Which issue was a major cause of the War of 1812?
questions.correctAnswer: British impressment of American sailors
distractors: Spanish attacks on Florida
French seizure of Louisiana
British support for Native American raids in Texas
questions.explanation: Britain's seizure of American sailors and interference with trade, plus pressure from War Hawks, pushed the U.S. to declare war in 1812.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Impressment - Britain grabbed our sailors, we grabbed our muskets!

questions.question: What did the Missouri Compromise of 1820 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Admitted Missouri as a slave state and Maine as a free state, and banned slavery north of 36-30 in the Louisiana Territory
distractors: Banned slavery in Missouri and Maine
Admitted both Missouri and Maine as slave states
Ended the slave trade in Washington, D.C.
questions.explanation: The compromise kept the Senate balanced and drew a line across the Louisiana Territory to limit slavery's expansion.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 36-30 line - Missouri slave, Maine free, and a line across the map!

questions.question: What was the spoils system under Andrew Jackson?
questions.correctAnswer: Giving government jobs to political supporters
distractors: Selling public land to the highest bidder
Dividing war booty among soldiers
Rewarding Native allies with territory
questions.explanation: Jackson replaced many federal officeholders with loyal supporters, arguing rotation in office was democratic.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Spoils system - to the victor belong the government jobs!

questions.question: What happened at the Seneca Falls Convention of 1848?
questions.correctAnswer: Women's rights activists issued the Declaration of Sentiments demanding equality
distractors: Abolitionists founded the Liberty Party
Temperance leaders banned alcohol in New York
Labor unions held their first national convention
questions.explanation: Organized by Elizabeth Cady Stanton and Lucretia Mott, Seneca Falls launched the organized women's rights movement in the U.S.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Seneca Falls 1848 - women declare sentiments, demand equality!

questions.question: What did the Kansas-Nebraska Act of 1854 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Let settlers decide slavery by popular sovereignty, repealing the Missouri Compromise line
distractors: Admitted Kansas and Nebraska as free states
Banned slavery in all western territories
Granted statehood to Kansas immediately
questions.explanation: Stephen Douglas's act opened the territories to popular sovereignty, leading to violent 'Bleeding Kansas' and the collapse of the Whig Party.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Kansas-Nebraska - let the settlers vote, and Kansas bled!

questions.question: What did the Dred Scott decision (1857) rule?
questions.correctAnswer: African Americans were not citizens and Congress could not ban slavery in the territories
distractors: Slavery was illegal in all U.S. territories
Escaped slaves had the right to a jury trial
Missouri could not remain a slave state
questions.explanation: Chief Justice Taney's ruling declared the Missouri Compromise unconstitutional and denied citizenship to Black Americans, deepening sectional conflict.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dred Scott - the Court said no citizenship, no limits on slavery!

questions.question: Which three amendments are known as the Reconstruction Amendments?
questions.correctAnswer: The 13th, 14th, and 15th Amendments
distractors: The 12th, 13th, and 14th Amendments
The 14th, 15th, and 16th Amendments
The 13th, 15th, and 17th Amendments
questions.explanation: The 13th abolished slavery, the 14th granted citizenship and equal protection, and the 15th protected voting rights regardless of race.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 13, 14, 15 - free them, make them citizens, let them vote!

questions.question: What did the Homestead Act of 1862 offer settlers?
questions.correctAnswer: 160 acres of public land for a small fee after five years of farming it
distractors: Free railroad passes to the West
Cash grants for building towns
Tax exemption for mining claims
questions.explanation: The act encouraged westward settlement by granting land to anyone who lived on and improved it for five years.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Homestead - 160 acres free if you farm it five years!

questions.question: What was the Populist movement of the 1890s mainly about?
questions.correctAnswer: Farmers demanding government help against railroads, banks, and low crop prices
distractors: Industrial workers demanding an eight-hour day
Immigrants demanding open borders
Southerners demanding the repeal of Reconstruction laws
questions.explanation: The People's Party called for free silver, railroad regulation, and a graduated income tax to help struggling farmers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Populists - farmers vs railroads, banks, and falling prices!

questions.question: What was a muckraker during the Progressive Era?
questions.correctAnswer: A journalist who exposed corruption and social problems
distractors: A politician who took bribes from corporations
A labor organizer who led strikes
A scientist who studied urban sanitation
questions.explanation: Muckrakers like Upton Sinclair (The Jungle) and Ida Tarbell exposed abuses, fueling reform laws on food, drugs, and trusts.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Muckrakers - journalists who raked the muck and exposed the rot!

questions.question: What were Woodrow Wilson's Fourteen Points mainly meant to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Outline a plan for a just peace after World War I
distractors: Justify American entry into the war
Divide Germany's colonies among the Allies
Create the United Nations
questions.explanation: Wilson's 1918 points called for open diplomacy, freedom of the seas, self-determination, and a League of Nations.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Fourteen Points - Wilson's recipe for peace without victory!

questions.question: What was the Red Scare of 1919-1920?
questions.correctAnswer: Fear of communism and radicalism that led to raids and deportations
distractors: A flu epidemic that killed millions
A wave of bank failures
A series of race riots in northern cities
questions.explanation: After the Russian Revolution, Attorney General Palmer's raids targeted suspected radicals and immigrants, violating civil liberties.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Red Scare - fear of reds led to raids and deportations!

questions.question: What was the Harlem Renaissance?
questions.correctAnswer: A flowering of African American literature, music, and art in 1920s Harlem
distractors: A political movement to return to Africa
A housing project in New York City
A labor strike by Black railroad workers
questions.explanation: Writers like Langston Hughes and musicians like Duke Ellington made Harlem the center of Black cultural life in the 1920s.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Harlem Renaissance - jazz, poetry, and pride in the 1920s!

questions.question: What caused the Dust Bowl of the 1930s?
questions.correctAnswer: Severe drought combined with poor farming practices on the Great Plains
distractors: Volcanic eruptions in the Rockies
Overgrazing by cattle ranchers alone
Flooding from the Mississippi River
questions.explanation: Drought plus overplowing stripped the topsoil, creating dust storms that forced many farm families to migrate west.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dust Bowl - dry soil and bad plows made black blizzards!

questions.question: What did the Lend-Lease Act of 1941 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Allowed the U.S. to lend or lease war supplies to Britain and other Allies
distractors: Drafted American soldiers for service in Europe
Banned trade with all warring nations
Sold the Philippines to Japan
questions.explanation: Lend-Lease made the U.S. the 'arsenal of democracy' before Pearl Harbor, supplying Britain, the USSR, and China.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lend-Lease - lend the guns now, settle the bill later!

questions.question: What was the Truman Doctrine of 1947?
questions.correctAnswer: The U.S. would support free peoples resisting communist pressure
distractors: The U.S. would build atomic bombs for its allies
The U.S. would withdraw from Europe
The U.S. would recognize communist China
questions.explanation: Truman pledged aid to Greece and Turkey and, more broadly, to contain communism, a policy that shaped the Cold War.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Truman Doctrine - help free peoples fight communism!

questions.question: What was the outcome of the Korean War (1950-1953)?
questions.correctAnswer: An armistice that left Korea divided near the 38th parallel
distractors: A unified Korea under the United Nations
A communist victory over South Korea
A peace treaty that ended the Cold War
questions.explanation: The war ended in a stalemate; North and South Korea remain divided today under a 1953 armistice, not a peace treaty.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Korea 1953 - armistice, not peace, and still divided!

questions.question: What happened during the Cuban Missile Crisis of 1962?
questions.correctAnswer: The U.S. discovered Soviet nuclear missiles in Cuba and imposed a naval quarantine
distractors: Cuba invaded Florida with Soviet help
The U.S. bombed missile sites in Cuba
The Soviet Union withdrew from the United Nations
questions.explanation: The 13-day standoff ended when the USSR agreed to remove the missiles and the U.S. pledged not to invade Cuba.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Thirteen days in October - missiles in Cuba, world holds its breath!

questions.question: What was Lyndon Johnson's Great Society?
questions.correctAnswer: A program of civil rights, anti-poverty, health, and education reforms in the 1960s
distractors: A plan to end the Vietnam War quickly
A tax cut for wealthy Americans
A program to build the interstate highway system
questions.explanation: The Great Society created Medicare, Medicaid, Head Start, and the War on Poverty alongside landmark civil rights laws.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Great Society - Medicare, Medicaid, and a war on poverty!

questions.question: What was the Tet Offensive of 1968?
questions.correctAnswer: A massive coordinated Viet Cong attack on South Vietnamese cities during a holiday truce
distractors: A U.S. bombing campaign against North Vietnam
A peace negotiation in Paris
A South Vietnamese invasion of Cambodia
questions.explanation: Although a military failure for the communists, Tet shocked Americans and turned public opinion against the war.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tet 1968 - a surprise attack that changed minds at home!

questions.question: What did the Camp David Accords of 1978 achieve?
questions.correctAnswer: A framework that led to a peace treaty between Egypt and Israel, brokered by Jimmy Carter
distractors: An end to the Iran hostage crisis
A nuclear arms agreement with the Soviet Union
A trade deal between the U.S. and Mexico
questions.explanation: Carter mediated between Anwar Sadat and Menachem Begin at Camp David in 1978. The accords themselves were a framework, not the treaty: they led to the 1979 Egypt-Israel peace treaty, under which Egypt became the first Arab state to recognize Israel.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Camp David - Carter, Sadat, Begin, and a handshake for peace!

questions.question: What was Reaganomics?
questions.correctAnswer: Supply-side policies of tax cuts, deregulation, and reduced domestic spending
distractors: A plan to nationalize major industries
A program of massive public works
A policy of raising taxes on the middle class
questions.explanation: Reagan's economic program argued that cutting taxes on businesses and the wealthy would spur investment and growth.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Reaganomics - cut taxes, deregulate, and let wealth trickle down!

questions.question: What was the Iran-Contra affair?
questions.correctAnswer: Secret arms sales to Iran used to fund Nicaraguan Contra rebels despite a congressional ban
distractors: A hostage rescue mission in Tehran
A trade embargo against Iran
A CIA plot to overthrow the Shah
questions.explanation: Reagan administration officials secretly sold arms to Iran and diverted the money to the Contras, violating the Boland Amendment.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Iran-Contra - arms for hostages, cash for Contras, scandal for all!

questions.question: What triggered the financial crisis of 2008?
questions.correctAnswer: The collapse of the housing bubble and risky mortgage-backed securities
distractors: A sudden spike in oil prices
The failure of the dot-com stock bubble
A trade war with China
questions.explanation: Subprime mortgages bundled into securities failed when housing prices fell, freezing credit and triggering the Great Recession.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 2008 - the housing bubble burst and the banks froze!

questions.question: What did the Affordable Care Act of 2010 mainly do?
questions.correctAnswer: Expanded health insurance coverage and regulated insurers
distractors: Created a single-payer national health system
Abolished Medicare and Medicaid
Made health insurance optional for employers only
questions.explanation: The ACA required most Americans to have coverage, expanded Medicaid, and barred insurers from denying coverage for pre-existing conditions.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Obamacare - more people covered, pre-existing conditions protected!

questions.question: What did the Sherman Antitrust Act of 1890 outlaw?
questions.correctAnswer: Monopolies and combinations in restraint of trade
distractors: Labor unions and strikes
Foreign ownership of railroads
Price-fixing by small businesses only
questions.explanation: The act was the first federal attempt to break up monopolies, though it was rarely used effectively until the Progressive Era.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Sherman 1890 - bust the trusts, free the trade!

questions.question: What did the Interstate Commerce Act of 1887 create?
questions.correctAnswer: Federal regulation of railroads through the Interstate Commerce Commission
distractors: A national highway system
The first federal income tax
A ban on railroad strikes
questions.explanation: It was the first federal regulatory agency, aimed at curbing railroad rate discrimination against farmers and small shippers.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Interstate Commerce - the first federal watchdog over the rails!

questions.question: What was the Open Door Policy toward China?
questions.correctAnswer: All nations should have equal trading rights in China
distractors: China should be closed to all foreign trade
The U.S. should annex Chinese ports
Only Britain could trade with China
questions.explanation: Secretary of State John Hay's 1899 notes asked European powers to keep China open to trade rather than carving it into exclusive spheres.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Open Door - keep China open for everyone's trade!

questions.question: Why was the Panama Canal important to the United States?
questions.correctAnswer: It shortened the sea route between the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans
distractors: It gave the U.S. control of the Suez Canal
It stopped European ships from reaching South America
It provided drinking water for Panama City
questions.explanation: Completed in 1914, the canal let ships avoid the long trip around South America and strengthened U.S. naval and commercial power.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Panama Canal - cut through the isthmus, cut weeks off the voyage!

questions.question: What was nativism in the 1920s?
questions.correctAnswer: Hostility toward immigrants and a push to restrict immigration
distractors: A movement to preserve Native American languages
A philosophy that favored rural over urban life
A campaign to ban foreign goods
questions.explanation: Nativism fueled the 1921 and 1924 quota laws that sharply limited immigration, especially from southern and eastern Europe and Asia.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nativism - fear of newcomers led to quota laws!

questions.question: What was the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA)?
questions.correctAnswer: A New Deal agency that built dams and brought electricity to a poor region
distractors: A program to relocate farmers to cities
A federal bank for southern states
A military base in Tennessee
questions.explanation: The TVA built dams for flood control and hydroelectric power, modernizing the Tennessee Valley and creating jobs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: TVA - dams, power, and jobs for the Tennessee Valley!

questions.question: What did the GI Bill of 1944 provide for World War II veterans?
questions.correctAnswer: Education benefits, low-interest home loans, and unemployment pay
distractors: Free cars and lifetime pensions
Guaranteed government jobs
Free land in the West
questions.explanation: The Servicemen's Readjustment Act helped millions of veterans attend college and buy homes, fueling the postwar boom.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: GI Bill - college, a home, and a fresh start for veterans!

questions.question: What was the Marshall Plan?
questions.correctAnswer: U.S. aid to rebuild Western Europe after World War II
distractors: A plan to divide Germany into four zones
A military alliance against the Soviet Union
A program to bring European scientists to America
questions.explanation: The 1948 plan gave over 12 billion dollars to rebuild European economies, aiming to prevent communism and restore trade.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Marshall Plan - rebuild Europe, stop communism, restart trade!

questions.question: What was NATO, founded in 1949?
questions.correctAnswer: A military alliance of the United States, Canada, and Western European nations
distractors: A trade agreement between the U.S. and Britain
A United Nations peacekeeping force
An organization to control nuclear weapons
questions.explanation: The North Atlantic Treaty Organization committed members to collective defense against Soviet aggression.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: NATO 1949 - an attack on one is an attack on all!

questions.question: What did the Civil Rights Act of 1964 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Banned discrimination in employment and public accommodations based on race, color, religion, sex, or national origin
distractors: Granted voting rights to all citizens over 18
Desegregated the military
Created the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission only
questions.explanation: The landmark law ended legal segregation in public places and outlawed employment discrimination, enforced by the federal government.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: 1964 - no more whites-only signs, no more job discrimination!

questions.question: What was the main argument of Federalist No. 10?
questions.correctAnswer: A large republic can control factions better than a small one
distractors: The states should have more power than the federal government
A bill of rights is unnecessary
The president should serve for life
questions.explanation: Madison argued that in an extended republic, many competing interests would prevent any single faction from dominating.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Federalist 10 - many factions cancel each other out in a big republic!

questions.question: What was the XYZ Affair of 1797-1798?
questions.correctAnswer: French agents demanded bribes from American diplomats, sparking an undeclared naval war
distractors: British agents plotted to seize New Orleans
Spanish officials closed the Mississippi River
Dutch merchants smuggled goods into New York
questions.explanation: The French demand for bribes outraged Americans, leading to the Quasi-War and the slogan 'Millions for defense, but not one cent for tribute.'
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: XYZ - French agents want bribes, America says no tribute!

questions.question: What was the Hartford Convention of 1814-1815?
questions.correctAnswer: New England Federalists met to discuss grievances over the War of 1812 and possible secession
distractors: A meeting that drafted the Monroe Doctrine
A convention that banned the slave trade
A gathering of abolitionists in Connecticut
questions.explanation: The convention's talk of secession discredited the Federalist Party when news of the Treaty of Ghent, which ended the war on status-quo terms, arrived together with news of Jackson's victory at the Battle of New Orleans, making the Federalists look disloyal.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Hartford - Federalists talk secession, then the war ends and they vanish!

questions.question: What was the Nullification Crisis of 1832-1833 about?
questions.correctAnswer: South Carolina claimed it could nullify a federal tariff it considered unconstitutional
distractors: Georgia refused to follow Supreme Court rulings on Native land
Virginia threatened to secede over the Missouri Compromise
Massachusetts refused to pay federal taxes
questions.explanation: Calhoun's doctrine of nullification clashed with Jackson's defense of the Union; a compromise tariff defused the crisis.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Nullification - South Carolina vs Jackson, Union wins this round!

questions.question: What did the Wilmot Proviso of 1846 propose?
questions.correctAnswer: Slavery would be banned in any territory acquired from Mexico
distractors: Texas would be annexed as a free state
California would be divided into two states
The slave trade would end in Washington, D.C.
questions.explanation: The proviso passed the House but not the Senate, and it sharpened the sectional debate over slavery in new territories.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wilmot Proviso - no slavery in the land won from Mexico!

questions.question: What was a key part of the Compromise of 1850?
questions.correctAnswer: California entered as a free state while a stronger Fugitive Slave Act was passed
distractors: Slavery was banned in all new territories
Texas was split into two states
The Missouri Compromise line was extended to the Pacific
questions.explanation: Henry Clay's compromise admitted California free, organized Utah and New Mexico by popular sovereignty, and tightened fugitive slave enforcement.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Compromise of 1850 - California free, but fugitives face a harsher law!

questions.question: What was the Freeport Doctrine?
questions.correctAnswer: Stephen Douglas's claim that territories could exclude slavery by refusing to pass laws protecting it
distractors: Lincoln's plan to free slaves in border states
A proposal to make Chicago a free port
A doctrine supporting the expansion of slavery into Cuba
questions.explanation: At Freeport in 1858, Douglas argued that popular sovereignty let territories keep slavery out in practice, which cost him Southern support in 1860.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Freeport - Douglas says territories can freeze slavery out by doing nothing!

questions.question: What was the Wade-Davis Bill of 1864?
questions.correctAnswer: A Radical Republican plan requiring a majority of white males to swear loyalty before a state could rejoin the Union
distractors: A law freeing slaves in border states
A bill creating the Freedmen's Bureau
A plan to divide the South into military districts
questions.explanation: Lincoln pocket-vetoed the bill because he favored a more lenient Reconstruction plan based on 10 percent loyalty oaths.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wade-Davis - Radicals demand half the South swear loyalty, Lincoln says no!

questions.question: What was the Credit Mobilier scandal?
questions.correctAnswer: A construction company bribed congressmen with discounted stock to protect its railroad contracts
distractors: A bank collapsed after lending to the government
A railroad company went bankrupt from overbuilding
A mining company cheated the Treasury of gold
questions.explanation: The Union Pacific's construction arm overcharged the government and bribed officials, damaging Grant's administration.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Credit Mobilier - railroad builders bribe Congress with cheap stock!

questions.question: What did the Bland-Allison Act of 1878 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Required the Treasury to buy and coin silver each month
distractors: Banned the coinage of silver entirely
Put the U.S. on the gold standard
Created the Federal Reserve
questions.explanation: The act was a compromise between free-silver advocates and gold supporters, mandating limited monthly silver purchases.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bland-Allison - buy some silver, please the farmers, keep the gold men calm!

questions.question: Why was the Pullman Strike of 1894 significant?
questions.correctAnswer: Federal troops broke the strike, showing government support for business over labor
distractors: It won workers an eight-hour day
It led to the founding of the AFL
It ended all railroad strikes for a decade
questions.explanation: When the American Railway Union boycotted Pullman cars, Attorney General Olney obtained an injunction and Cleveland sent troops, crushing the strike and jailing Eugene Debs.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Pullman 1894 - troops break the boycott, labor loses this round!

questions.question: What did Plessy v. Ferguson (1896) establish?
questions.correctAnswer: The 'separate but equal' doctrine legalizing segregation
distractors: The right of states to ban interracial marriage
The unconstitutionality of Jim Crow laws
The federal power to integrate schools
questions.explanation: The Court upheld Louisiana's segregated railroad cars, giving legal cover to segregation until Brown v. Board in 1954.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Plessy 1896 - separate but equal, the law of segregation!

questions.question: What did the Insular Cases (1901) decide?
questions.correctAnswer: The Constitution does not automatically extend full rights to people in newly acquired territories
distractors: Puerto Rico and the Philippines must become states
The U.S. could not acquire overseas territory
All territorial residents were full citizens
questions.explanation: The Court ruled that only some constitutional rights applied in 'unincorporated' territories like Puerto Rico and the Philippines.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Insular Cases - the flag flies there, but the Constitution follows only partly!

questions.question: What was the Teapot Dome scandal?
questions.correctAnswer: The Secretary of the Interior secretly leased federal oil reserves for bribes
distractors: A cabinet member sold military secrets to Germany
A senator embezzled funds from the Treasury
A governor rigged elections with oil money
questions.explanation: Albert Fall leased Navy oil reserves at Teapot Dome, Wyoming, to private companies for bribes, the first cabinet secretary jailed for a crime in office.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Teapot Dome - oil reserves leased for bribes, a secretary goes to jail!

questions.question: What was the effect of the Smoot-Hawley Tariff of 1930?
questions.correctAnswer: It raised tariffs sharply and worsened the Depression by shrinking world trade
distractors: It lowered prices for American consumers
It ended the Depression by protecting farmers
It encouraged other nations to lower their tariffs
questions.explanation: The tariff raised duties to record levels, prompting retaliation that cut international trade by two-thirds and deepened the Depression.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Smoot-Hawley - high tariffs, trade war, deeper Depression!

questions.question: What was Roosevelt's court-packing plan of 1937?
questions.correctAnswer: A proposal to add justices to the Supreme Court after it struck down New Deal laws
distractors: A plan to remove justices who opposed the New Deal
A law limiting the Court to nine members
A proposal to elect Supreme Court justices
questions.explanation: FDR proposed adding one justice for each over 70, up to six, to gain a favorable Court. Congress rejected it, though the Court soon upheld New Deal laws.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Court-packing - FDR tries to add judges, Congress says no!

questions.question: What did the Yalta Conference of February 1945 agree on?
questions.correctAnswer: Postwar division of Germany, Soviet entry into the war against Japan, and the United Nations
distractors: An immediate invasion of Japan
The creation of NATO
The unconditional surrender of Italy
questions.explanation: Roosevelt, Churchill, and Stalin agreed on occupation zones, a new world organization, and Soviet promises on Poland and Japan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Yalta - divide Germany, plan the UN, promise to fight Japan!

questions.question: What ended Senator Joseph McCarthy's influence in 1954?
questions.correctAnswer: The televised Army-McCarthy hearings exposed his bullying tactics
distractors: He lost his Senate re-election
President Eisenhower fired him
The Supreme Court ruled his investigations illegal
questions.explanation: During the hearings, Army counsel Joseph Welch asked 'Have you no sense of decency?' and the Senate censured McCarthy later that year.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Army-McCarthy - have you no sense of decency, sir!

questions.question: What did the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution of 1964 do?
questions.correctAnswer: Gave President Johnson broad authority to use military force in Vietnam
distractors: Declared war on North Vietnam
Authorized the bombing of Cambodia
Ended U.S. involvement in Southeast Asia
questions.explanation: After reported attacks on U.S. destroyers, Congress passed the resolution, which Johnson used as a blank check for escalation.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Tonkin - a resolution that became a blank check for war!

questions.question: What did the War Powers Act of 1973 require?
questions.correctAnswer: The president must notify Congress within 48 hours of deploying troops and withdraw them after 60 days without approval
distractors: Congress must declare war before any troops deploy
The president cannot deploy troops overseas at all
The military must report directly to Congress
questions.explanation: Passed over Nixon's veto after Vietnam, the act aimed to restore Congress's war powers, though presidents have disputed its constitutionality.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: War Powers - 48 hours to tell Congress, 60 days to get approval!

questions.question: What was the SALT II treaty of 1979 about?
questions.correctAnswer: Limiting strategic nuclear weapons between the U.S. and the Soviet Union
distractors: Banning all nuclear testing
Reducing conventional forces in Europe
Sharing missile defense technology
questions.explanation: Carter and Brezhnev signed SALT II to cap nuclear launchers, but the Senate never ratified it after the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: SALT II - cap the missiles, but Afghanistan kills the treaty!

questions.question: What did Regents of the University of California v. Bakke (1978) decide?
questions.correctAnswer: Racial quotas in admissions are unconstitutional, but race may be one factor among many
distractors: Affirmative action is entirely unconstitutional
Universities must admit students by test scores alone
States cannot consider race in any public policy
questions.explanation: The Court struck down UC Davis's quota system but allowed race as a 'plus factor' in admissions, a compromise that shaped affirmative action for decades.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Bakke - no quotas, but race can count as one factor!

questions.question: What was the Gramm-Rudman-Hollings Act of 1985 designed to do?
questions.correctAnswer: Force automatic spending cuts to reduce the federal budget deficit
distractors: Raise taxes to balance the budget
Create a balanced budget amendment
Abolish the national debt
questions.explanation: The act set deficit targets enforced by automatic sequestration, but the Supreme Court struck down its enforcement mechanism in 1986.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Gramm-Rudman - hit the deficit target or the budget gets cut automatically!

questions.question: What did the USA PATRIOT Act of 2001 expand?
questions.correctAnswer: Government surveillance and law enforcement powers to fight terrorism
distractors: The military draft for the war in Afghanistan
Border wall construction along Mexico
The power of states to deport immigrants
questions.explanation: Passed after 9/11, the act expanded wiretapping, search, and detention powers, raising debates about civil liberties versus security.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: PATRIOT Act - more surveillance powers after 9/11!

questions.question: What did Citizens United v. FEC (2010) decide?
questions.correctAnswer: Corporate and union spending on elections is protected free speech
distractors: Corporations cannot donate to candidates
Campaign finance limits are unconstitutional in all cases
Only individuals may fund political ads
questions.explanation: The Court ruled that restricting independent political spending by corporations violated the First Amendment, reshaping campaign finance.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Citizens United - corporate money talks, and the Court calls it speech!

questions.question: What was the Dawes Act of 1887 meant to do to Native Americans?
questions.correctAnswer: Break up tribal lands into individual allotments to encourage assimilation
distractors: Grant tribes full sovereignty over their lands
Create reservations for all tribes in Oklahoma
Pay tribes for land taken by settlers
questions.explanation: The act divided communal tribal land into 160-acre allotments, with 'surplus' sold to settlers, costing tribes about two-thirds of their land by 1934.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Dawes Act - split the tribal land, sell the surplus, erase the tribe!

questions.question: What happened at Wounded Knee in 1890?
questions.correctAnswer: U.S. soldiers killed about 150 Lakota Sioux, ending armed Native resistance on the Plains
distractors: The Sioux defeated the U.S. Army in battle
A treaty granted the Sioux the Black Hills
The Ghost Dance movement began
questions.explanation: The massacre followed the army's attempt to disarm Lakota practicing the Ghost Dance and marked the end of the Indian Wars era.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Wounded Knee 1890 - a massacre that closed the frontier wars!

questions.question: What was the Lowell mill system?
questions.correctAnswer: Textile factories in Massachusetts that employed young farm women living in company boardinghouses
distractors: A system of slave labor in southern cotton mills
A network of canals built by Irish immigrants
A plan to unionize all New England factories
questions.explanation: Lowell's mills recruited 'mill girls' from farm families, offering wages and supervised housing, an early model of American industrial labor.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Lowell mills - farm girls become factory workers, dorms included!

questions.question: What reform movements grew out of the Second Great Awakening?
questions.correctAnswer: Abolition, temperance, women's rights, and prison and education reform
distractors: Only the abolition movement
Socialism and anarchism
The Populist and Progressive movements
questions.explanation: The religious revival of the 1820s-1840s inspired Americans to perfect society through reform, linking evangelical faith to social activism.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Second Great Awakening - revival fires up reform in every direction!

questions.question: What was the policy of containment and its key document NSC-68?
questions.correctAnswer: A strategy to stop the spread of communism, with NSC-68 calling for a major military buildup
distractors: A plan to contain the Soviet Union by trade embargoes alone
A policy of withdrawing from all overseas bases
A strategy to overthrow communist governments by force
questions.explanation: George Kennan proposed containment in 1947. NSC-68, drafted in April 1950 before the Korean War began, called for a major military buildup to apply containment globally; Truman approved and funded that buildup only after North Korea invaded the South in June 1950.
questions.memoryHook: T-Rexy says: Containment - stop communism from spreading, then build the muscle to do it!
